name: Matrimony.com Ltd
title: Matrimony.com Ltd - 540704 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Matrimony.com Q1 FY27 PAT rose 127.5% YoY to Rs 19.1 crore on consolidated revenue of Rs 130.5 crore (+13.2% YoY).
summary.overview: Consolidated billing was Rs 136.0 crore (+7.8% QoQ and +7.8% YoY) and revenue Rs 130.5 crore (+11.7% QoQ, +13.2% YoY), with consolidated EBITDA margin of 20.1% versus 12.4% in Q4 and 11% a year ago. Matchmaking EBITDA margin rose to 26.9%, helped by deferred revenue from last year's introduction of a one-year package. Management guided Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to double-digit YoY growth and PAT to triple-digit YoY growth, with profit similar to or slightly above Q1. The non-matchmaking wedding services business remained loss-making (EBITDA loss Rs 3.8 crore) and is being shifted from subscription to a commission model.

segments.name: Matchmaking
segments.commentary: Billing Rs 135.3 crore (+8.0% YoY) and revenue Rs 109.5 crore (+13.6% YoY); EBITDA Rs 34.9 crore at 26.9% margin. Management said EBITDA would have been about Rs 40 crore had billing equalled revenue.

segments.name: Marriage services and other businesses
segments.commentary: Billing Rs 74 lakh (-13.8% YoY, +0.5% QoQ) and revenue Rs 96 lakh (-24.3% YoY, +13.1% QoQ); EBITDA loss Rs 3.8 crore. Q4 included an impairment, which management said drove the higher loss.

guidance_outlook: Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to grow double digits YoY.
Q2 PAT to grow triple digits YoY; profit expected at a similar level to Q1 or slightly better.
Marriage services billing expected to be higher in Q1 than in the current quarter (management said Q2 billing would exceed Q1).
Revenue-to-billing conversion expected at roughly 96-99% in a given quarter, depending on billing mix.
Wedding services targeted at a Rs 100 crore run rate before it contributes to profit; management said clarity likely in about a year.
capex_capacity: Marketing spend to be held and slightly stepped up to support growth and new initiatives such as love.com and Malayalee Love.
Manyjobs remains focused on Tamil Nadu; national expansion not planned until next year or later, and it needs a run rate before breakeven.
Goodwill impairment was taken in Q4; further impairment depends on the performance of the newer businesses.
Rs 4 crore invested in an AI astrology startup (Bharat Ek Khoj) as a long-term investment.
demand_pricing: Paid subscriptions added: 2.72 lakh in the quarter (+15.9% QoQ, +3.7% YoY).
Matchmaking ATV fell 6.7% QoQ but rose 4.2% YoY; management said ATV should not be read too much into, citing package mix, discounts and the Jodi and love.com low-price products.
No ASP or ticket price increase planned; pricing handled through segmentation and analytics.
One-year package is a small share of users; management said it is individual choice and not an incentive lever.
Over 25,500 success stories in the quarter.
Management said it is not seeing a reduction in competitive ad intensity but is not fully slowing down; plans to slightly step up marketing.

qa_highlights.question: How is revenue recognised and how big is the billing-revenue gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised over the membership period (3 months to 1 year). The gap was about Rs 5 crore in Q1 and is expected to be Rs 3-5 crore on an ongoing basis, mainly due to the one-year package introduced last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the triple-digit profit growth sustainable, given flat revenue in recent quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the jump to continued growth plus deferred revenue from the one-year package introduced last year, and guided Q2 PAT to a similar or slightly higher level than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for AI, growth and investor presentation data?
qa_highlights.answer: AI is used for profile and photo validation, chatbots and product work. Growth comes from profile acquisition, conversion and launches such as love.com and regional versions. Management agreed to update the investor presentation data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ATV falling and will ASPs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ATV is not in a steady state, citing segment, package and discount mix plus low-priced Jodi and love.com products. There are no plans for a ticket price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Wedding services: break-even timeline and ad spend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on reaching a Rs 100 crore run rate rather than breakeven, with a commission model being piloted. It expects marketing to be held or stepped up slightly rather than cut.

qa_highlights.question: Legal fees increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sushanta Swain said the rise is from registering a large number of trademarks to prevent misuse.

risks_watch: Revenue quality: Q2 profit guidance depends on deferred revenue from the one-year package, and ATV fell 6.7% QoQ.
Marriage services: still loss-making, with the commission model unproven and a Rs 100 crore run rate target about a year away.
Marketing intensity: matchmaking marketing spend rose to Rs 46.5 crore and management plans a slight step-up.
Impairment risk on the newer businesses after the Q4 goodwill impairment.
Management declined to disclose business split, geography mix and whether there will be any cash deployment (acquisition or shareholder reward).
summary.management_tone: Confident on matchmaking profitability and Q2 guidance, but evasive on pricing, geography, segment split and capital deployment, citing competitive reasons. Cautious on wedding services, described as still in piloting with no firm breakeven timeline.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we have delivered on that guidance with the PAT increasing by 127% year-on-year.
So, I think Matchmaking has reached a certain level of threshold in terms of EBITDA margins.
We changed the model which we communicated some time back. We moved from the subscription business model to a commission-led model.

adds.what: Rs 4 crore investment in AI astrology startup Bharat Ek Khoj (long-term investment, not capacity)

growth.why: Q1 revenue rose 13.2% YoY and management guided Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to grow double digits YoY with PAT growing triple digits, but no physical capacity is being added and the company's own pricing and marketing spend is held or only slightly stepped up.
